items.title: Finite statistical microstate model
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
A finite statistical microstate model is a pair $(\Omega,\epsilon)$ where $\Omega$ is a finite nonempty set and $\epsilon:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ assigns a finite numerical energy to each microstate. The physical energy of $x\in\Omega$ is $E(x)=\epsilon(x)\,\mathrm J$, with its zero and any retained internal offsets fixed by the declared material model. Energies are evaluated in the center-of-mass rest frame specified by [[def-td-galilean-rest-frame]], and $U$ is the corresponding macroscopic internal-energy coordinate of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. Equal energy values at distinct elements of $\Omega$ count as distinct microstates.

When two such models are declared independent, their joint microstate set is the Cartesian product $\Omega_A\times\Omega_B$, and additivity of the microscopic energy is the explicit condition $\epsilon_{AB}(x,y)=\epsilon_A(x)+\epsilon_B(y)$. Independence and this energy equation are model data; they do not follow merely from the two systems being separated. The definition itself assigns no weights, temperature, probability law, or dynamics.

items.title: Regular Hamiltonian shell preparation data
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Fix an integer $n\ge1$, a canonical chart with physical coordinates $q_i$ in metres and $p_i$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, and the corresponding dimensionless coordinates $\hat q_i=q_i/(1\,\mathrm m)$ and $\hat p_i=p_i/(1\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}})$. Let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^{2n}$ be the open domain of the numerical vector $\hat x=(\hat q,\hat p)$, let $\hat H:O	o\mathbb R$ be the numerical energy map with physical energy $H=(1\,\mathrm J)\hat H$, and require $\hat H$ to have continuous partial derivatives through order two. A specified open interval $J_E\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a regular compact-shell band when $\hat H^{-1}(K)$ is compact in $O$ for every compact $K\subset J_E$ and $
abla\hat H$ is nonzero at every point of $\hat H^{-1}(J_E)$.

For $\hat E\in J_E$, the energy shell is $\Sigma_{\hat E}:=\{x\in O:\hat H(x)=\hat E\}$. The graph-chart definition of the weighted shell integral is [[def-tdmath-regular-energy-shell]]: in a local graph chart $x_i=h(z,\hat E)$, its coarea measure is $d\mu_{\hat E}=dA_{\hat E}/|
abla\hat H|$, with graph-area factor and gradient in the dimensionless Euclidean coordinates. Set $D(\hat E):=\int_{\Sigma_{\hat E}}d\mu_{\hat E}$ and admit the preparation only when $\Sigma_{\hat E}
e\varnothing$ and $0<D(\hat E)<\infty$. Its normalized shell law is $
u_{\hat E}(A):=D(\hat E)^{-1}\mu_{\hat E}(A\cap\Sigma_{\hat E})$. The current draft theorem [[thm-tdmath-regular-energy-shell-measure]] proves the coarea identity, chart independence and positive finite shell mass under its stated $C^2$, compact-regular-band hypotheses; its statement and proof are present, while its acceptance remains unresolved. Multiplying the unnormalized shell measure by a fixed positive phase-volume normalization does not change $
u_{\hat E}$.

items.title: Canonical sampling assumption for finite and normalized statistical models
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Assign a positive temperature $T$ in kelvins and the exact framework constant $k_{\mathrm B}$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ from [[def-td-si-quantities]], and put $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$. For a finite microstate model $(\Omega,\epsilon)$, adopt the canonical preparation
$$P_\beta(x)=\frac{e^{-\beta E(x)}}{Z(\beta)},\qquad Z(\beta)=\sum_{x\in\Omega}e^{-\beta E(x)}.$$
Here $Z$ is dimensionless, positive, and finite because $\Omega$ is finite and nonempty.

The same adopted law may be assigned to a specified countable state model with its stated enumeration and energy list, or to a measurable model $(X,\Sigma,\mu,E)$ with a dimensionless reference measure $\mu$ and measurable energy $E:X\to\mathbb R\,\mathrm J$, only when $0<Z(\beta)<\infty$ for the declared series or integral. In those cases $P_\beta(i)=e^{-\beta E_i}/Z$ or the probability density is $p_\beta=e^{-\beta E}/Z$ relative to $\mu$. The countable and integral conventions are those of [[def-tdmath-countable-canonical-model]] and [[def-tdmath-measure-integral]] at their actual current draft statements.

This is an adopted statistical-mechanical preparation rule. It is not derived from the macroscopic thermodynamic laws, a finite bath, entropy maximization, or a time-evolution equation. It does not assert that a physical sample has this preparation; that identification is an additional model assumption to be tested against a specified preparation and apparatus.

items.title: Microcanonical sampling assumption
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
For a finite microstate model and a declared energy value $E_0$ in joules and resolution $\delta\ge0$ in joules, define the admitted window
$$\Omega_{E_0,\delta}:=\{x\in\Omega:|E(x)-E_0|\le\delta\}.$$
When this set is nonempty, adopt the uniform preparation $P(x)=|\Omega_{E_0,\delta}|^{-1}$ on it and zero outside. Its dimensionless Boltzmann entropy is $\log|\Omega_{E_0,\delta}|$, and its physical entropy convention is $k_{\mathrm B}\log|\Omega_{E_0,\delta}|$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. A zero-width window is allowed only when it contains at least one microstate.

For a continuous classical model, when the hypotheses and normalization in [[def-td-regular-hamiltonian-shell-preparation]] hold, the microcanonical preparation is the normalized shell measure $\nu_{\hat E}$ defined there. These finite-window and regular-shell rules are adopted model preparations. They do not assert Hamiltonian ergodicity, equality with long-time averages, canonical sampling, or equilibration.

items.title: Countable canonical identities under a local moment envelope
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Let $I$ be a specified nonempty countable microstate list with energies $E_i$ in joules, counted once, and let $J_\beta\subset(0,\infty)$ be open. For $\beta\in J_\beta$, define $Z(\beta)=\sum_i e^{-\beta E_i}$ and, when $0<Z(\beta)<\infty$, $p_i(\beta)=e^{-\beta E_i}/Z(\beta)$. Suppose every compact interval $K\subset J_\beta$ admits a summable sequence $a_i\ge0$ with $(1+|E_i|^2)e^{-\beta E_i}\le a_i$ for all $i$ and $\beta\in K$. Then $Z$ is $C^2$, $-\partial_\beta\log Z=\bar E_\beta$, $\partial_\beta^2\log Z=\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E)$, and the dimensionless Gibbs entropy is finite with
$$-\sum_i p_i\log p_i=\log Z+\beta\bar E_\beta.$$
Thus $F_{\mathrm{stat}}=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z=\bar E_\beta-TS_\beta$ for $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$. A lower bound on the energies alone does not supply the summable envelope or finite partition function.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A specified countable energy list, a positive finite canonical partition sum on $J_\beta$, and the local summable second-moment envelope.

[F1] [[def-tdmath-countable-canonical-model]]: $I$ has a specified enumeration, $Z=\sum_i e^{-\beta E_i}$ uses the nonnegative series convention, and $p_i$ and expectations are defined only when $0<Z<\infty$.

[F2] [[post-td-canonical-sampling]]: for this normalized countable model, $p_i=e^{-\beta E_i}/Z$ is the adopted preparation law.

[L1] [[thm-tdmath-summable-canonical-differentiation]] (current batch 11 draft): under the local envelope $(1+|E_i|^2)e^{-\beta E_i}\le a_i$ on each compact interval, the normalized series has the stated $C^2$, mean, variance, and entropy identities. Its full current proof was inspected; its draft status remains conditional.

[F3] [[def-td-si-quantities]]: $E_i$ and $\bar E_\beta$ are in joules, $T$ is in kelvins, and $k_{\mathrm B}$ is in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, so $\beta$ is in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$.

[A1] The energy list and degeneracy convention are fixed while $\beta$ varies; every compact interval in $J_\beta$ has the stated summable envelope.

## Proof

**Given:** The countable model and its local envelope on the open interval $J_\beta$.

1.1 The assumptions in the Statement are exactly the countable model and envelope required by [L1]; the weights are counting weights, so each listed state contributes one factor $e^{-\beta E_i}$. By [F2], their normalized law is the adopted canonical preparation, and [F3] gives the SI dimensions. [F1, F2, F3, L1, A1]

2.1 Apply [L1] to this model: $Z\in C^2$, its logarithmic derivatives give the mean and variance, and the absolutely convergent entropy sum equals $\log Z+\beta\bar E_\beta$. Multiplying the entropy identity by $k_{\mathrm B}$ and using $\beta k_{\mathrm B}=1/T$ yields $F_{\mathrm{stat}}=\bar E_\beta-TS_\beta=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z$. The claim remains conditional on the draft supplier's proof and the envelope. [F2, F3, L1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Energy-density concentration at differentiable lattice pressure
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
For the lattice model and canonical law of [[pthm-td-lattice-bulk-pressure]], let $p_L(\gamma)=L^{-d}\log Z_L(\gamma)$ converge pointwise on an open interval $J_\beta\subset(0,\infty)$ to $p(\gamma)$. If $p$ is differentiable at $\beta\in J_\beta$, set $e=-p'(\beta)$ in joules per site. Then the canonical mean energy density satisfies $\mathbb E_{\beta,L}[H_L]/L^d\to e$, and for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exist $c>0$ and $L_0$ such that
$$\mathbb P_{\beta,L}\!\left(\left|H_L/L^d-e\right|\ge\varepsilon\right)\le2e^{-cL^d}\qquad(L\ge L_0).$$
The probability is the model's finite-volume canonical probability, not an observed frequency. No conclusion is asserted when $p$ is nondifferentiable.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The bounded finite-range lattice models, their canonical probabilities, pointwise convergence of $p_L$ on an open positive interval, and differentiability of the limit at $\beta$.

[F1] [[pthm-td-lattice-bulk-pressure]]: $p_L=L^{-d}\log Z_L$ is the reduced lattice log-partition density and its canonical law is the finite-volume model law.

[L1] [[thm-tdmath-limiting-derivative-and-concentration]] (current batch 11 draft): if the finite-volume lattice pressures converge pointwise on an open positive interval and the limiting pressure is differentiable at $\beta$, then the finite-volume mean energy density converges to $-p'(\beta)$ and both tails have an exponential bound. Its full current proof was inspected; its draft status remains conditional.

[F2] [[post-td-canonical-sampling]]: the finite-volume probabilities are $e^{-\beta H_L}/Z_L$.

[F3] [[def-td-si-quantities]]: $H_L$ and $e$ are in joules per site, $\beta$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, and the probability bound is dimensionless.

[A1] $\beta$ lies in an open interval $J_\beta\subset(0,\infty)$, $p_L\to p$ on that interval, and $p$ is differentiable at the specified $\beta$.

## Proof

**Given:** The lattice model, its finite canonical law, the pointwise limiting pressure, and differentiability at $\beta$.

1.1 The finite-volume energy law and $p_L$ in [F1]–[F2] match the model and probability hypotheses of [L1]. The condition $\beta>0$ and differentiability at $\beta$ are exactly those in [A1]. [F1, F2, F3, L1, A1]

2.1 Applying [L1] yields $\mathbb E_{\beta,L}[H_L]/L^d\to -p'(\beta)=e$ and, for each fixed $\varepsilon>0$, a constant $c>0$ and threshold $L_0$ with the stated two-tail exponential estimate. The result is a model probability statement and is silent at pressure nondifferentiability. [F1, L1, step 1.1] ∎

Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.4.6 and 6.2.2 (printed pp. 207–208 and 330–333)

items.title: Finite-bath canonical error under a smooth shell-entropy model
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Let the subsystem have a finite nonempty state set $\Omega$ and internal energies $E_x$ in joules with $|E_x|\le L$. A bath has a dimensionless shell entropy $s_B(u)$, defined on an open interval containing $[u_0-L,u_0+L]$ in joules, with $s_B\in C^2$ and $|s_B''(u)|\le M$ there; the model adopts $\beta=s'_B(u_0)>0$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$ and $T=(k_{\mathrm B}\beta)^{-1}$. Assume weak additive coupling and microcanonical shell sampling induce subsystem weights $P_B(x)\propto e^{s_B(u_0-E_x)}$. Let $P_C(x)=e^{-\beta E_x}/Z$ be the corresponding canonical law. With $\delta=ML^2/2$ (dimensionless), the shell log-weight remainder obeys
$$|s_B(u_0-E_x)-s_B(u_0)+\beta E_x|\le\delta,$$
and the normalized laws satisfy
$$\sum_{x\in\Omega}|P_B(x)-P_C(x)|\le e^{2\delta}-1.$$
This is an $\ell^1$ probability-vector bound; it does not assert a universal error or a thermodynamic limit.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The finite subsystem, the bath entropy and curvature bound, the adopted energy-additive shell model, and the two normalized laws.

[F1] [[def-td-finite-microstate-model]]: $\Omega$ is finite and nonempty and each $E_x$ is a fixed internal energy in joules.

[F2] [[post-td-canonical-sampling]]: the canonical comparison law has weights $e^{-\beta E_x}/Z$ when $Z>0$ is finite.

[F3] [[post-td-microcanonical-sampling]]: the microcanonical joint-shell model assigns the subsystem marginal induced by the bath shell weights when the weak-additive-coupling and shell hypotheses are imposed.

[L1] [[thm-tdmath-finite-bath-error-bound]] (current batch 11 draft): for finite energies $|E_x|\le L$, $s_B\in C^2$ on the stated interval, $|s_B''|\le M$, $\beta=s'_B(u_0)$, and normalized weights proportional to $e^{s_B(u_0-E_x)}$, the Taylor remainder is at most $\delta=ML^2/2$ and the canonical comparison law has $\ell^1$ error at most $e^{2\delta}-1$. Its full current proof was inspected; its draft status remains conditional.

[A1] $L,M\ge0$, $\beta>0$, the bath interval contains every $u_0-E_x$, and the physical energy unit is joules, so $\beta E_x$, $s_B$, and $\delta$ are dimensionless.

## Proof

**Given:** The finite-system energies, the smooth bath shell-entropy model, and the weak-additive microcanonical marginal stipulated in the Statement.

1.1 With $|E_x|\le L$, every bath argument $u_0-E_x$ lies in the stated interval. The curvature bound and $\beta=s'_B(u_0)$ therefore match the hypotheses of [L1], including the dimensionless remainder scale $\delta=ML^2/2$. The shell weights in [F3] are exactly the weights required by [L1], and the finite canonical comparison is [F2]. [F1, F2, F3, L1, A1]

2.1 Applying [L1] to these matched inputs gives $|s_B(u_0-E_x)-s_B(u_0)+\beta E_x|\le\delta$ for each state and $\sum_x|P_B(x)-P_C(x)|\le e^{2\delta}-1$. The claim is conditional on the actual shell-weight rule and the draft mathematical supplier, not on bath size alone. [F2, F3, L1, step 1.1] ∎

items.title: Finite canonical partition, energy, variance, entropy and free-energy identities
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Let $(\Omega,\epsilon)$ be a finite microstate model with energies $E_x=\epsilon(x)\,\mathrm J$ from [[def-td-finite-microstate-model]]. Let $T>0$, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$, and $P_\beta(x)=e^{-\beta E_x}/Z(\beta)$ be the adopted preparation of [[post-td-canonical-sampling]]. With $\bar E_\beta=\sum_xP_\beta(x)E_x$, $\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E)=\sum_xP_\beta(x)(E_x-\bar E_\beta)^2$, and $S_\beta=-k_{\mathrm B}\sum_xP_\beta(x)\log P_\beta(x)$, the finite partition sum is positive and
$$-\partial_\beta\log Z=\bar E_\beta,\qquad \partial_\beta^2\log Z=\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E),\qquad S_\beta=k_{\mathrm B}(\log Z+\beta\bar E_\beta).$$
Consequently the statistical free-energy value $F_{\mathrm{stat}}:=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z$ satisfies $F_{\mathrm{stat}}=\bar E_\beta-TS_\beta$. The derivatives hold the finite state set and its energy list fixed. No equivalence with a macroscopic entropy or Helmholtz potential is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A finite nonempty state set, a fixed energy list in joules, $T>0$, the fixed SI value of $k_{\mathrm B}$, and the adopted canonical weights.

[F1] [[def-td-finite-microstate-model]]: $\Omega$ is finite and nonempty and each $E_x$ is a fixed energy in joules.

[F2] [[post-td-canonical-sampling]]: $P_\beta(x)=e^{-\beta E_x}/Z$ with $Z=\sum_xe^{-\beta E_x}$ and $\beta=1/(k_{\mathrm B}T)>0$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$.

[F3] [[thm-derivative-of-exponential]]: $\frac{d}{d\beta}e^{-\beta E_x}=-E_xe^{-\beta E_x}$ for each fixed $E_x$.

[F4] [[thm-logarithm-derivative-and-integral]] and [[def-natural-logarithm]]: for differentiable positive $Z$, $(\log Z)'=Z'/Z$.

## Proof

**Given:** The finite canonical model and its fixed energy values.

1.1 Since $\Omega$ is finite and nonempty and every $e^{-\beta E_x}>0$, the finite sum $Z=\sum_xe^{-\beta E_x}$ is strictly positive and finite. The weights $P_\beta(x)$ therefore sum to one by their definition. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 Differentiating the finite sum term by term using [F3] gives $Z'=-\sum_xE_xe^{-\beta E_x}$ and $Z''=\sum_xE_x^2e^{-\beta E_x}$. Applying [F4] yields $-\partial_\beta\log Z=-(Z'/Z)=\bar E_\beta$ and $\partial_\beta^2\log Z=Z''/Z-(Z'/Z)^2=\sum_xP_\beta(x)E_x^2-\bar E_\beta^2=\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E)$. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1]

3.1 For each $x$, $\log P_\beta(x)=-\beta E_x-\log Z$. Substituting this into the finite entropy sum gives $S_\beta=-k_{\mathrm B}\sum_xP_\beta(x)\log P_\beta(x)=k_{\mathrm B}(\beta\bar E_\beta+\log Z)$. Since $\beta k_{\mathrm B}=1/T$, rearrangement gives $\bar E_\beta-TS_\beta=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z=F_{\mathrm{stat}}$. [F2, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.4–4.6 (printed pp. 205–217)

items.title: Canonical weights uniquely maximize finite-state entropy at their mean energy
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Let $(\Omega,\epsilon)$ be a finite nonempty microstate model, let $T>0$, and let $q_x=e^{-\beta E_x}/Z$ be its canonical probabilities at $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$. Set $\bar E=\sum_xq_xE_x$. Among all probability vectors $r=(r_x)_{x\in\Omega}$ with $\sum_xr_x=1$ and $\sum_xr_xE_x=\bar E$, the Shannon entropy $S(r):=-k_{\mathrm B}\sum_{x:r_x>0}r_x\log r_x$ is uniquely maximized by $r=q$. This is a finite-model variational theorem; it does not establish that a physical sample is prepared canonically.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A finite nonempty state set with fixed energies $E_x$ in joules, $T>0$, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$, the canonical law $q$, and a competing probability vector $r$ with the same mean energy.

[F1] [[def-td-finite-microstate-model]]: $\Omega$ is finite and nonempty and $E_x$ is fixed.

[F2] [[post-td-canonical-sampling]]: $q_x=e^{-\beta E_x}/Z$ with $q_x>0$ and $\sum_xq_x=1$.

[F3] [[pthm-td-finite-canonical-identities]]: $\bar E=\sum_xq_xE_x$ and $\log q_x=-\beta E_x-\log Z$.

[F4] [[thm-logarithm-derivative-and-integral]] and [[def-natural-logarithm]]: $\log t=\int_1^tdu/u$ for $t>0$.

[A1] The competitor has $r_x\ge0$, $\sum_xr_x=1$, and $\sum_xr_xE_x=\bar E$.

## Proof

**Given:** The finite model, its canonical weights, and a competing probability vector with the same mean.

1.1 For every $t>0$, [F4] gives $\log t\le t-1$, with equality only at $t=1$: for $t>1$, integrate $1/u<1$ on $(1,t)$; for $0<t<1$, integrate $1/u>1$ on $(t,1)$ and reverse the endpoints. For every $x$ with $r_x>0$, apply this to $t=q_x/r_x$ to obtain $r_x\log(r_x/q_x)\ge r_x-q_x$. Summing over the support of $r$ gives $D:=\sum_{x:r_x>0}r_x\log(r_x/q_x)\ge1-\sum_{x:r_x>0}q_x\ge0$. Equality forces full support and $r_x=q_x$ for every state. [F2, F4, A1, algebra]

2.1 Using [F3] and the fixed-mean condition [A1], $D=\sum_{x:r_x>0}r_x\log r_x+\beta\bar E+\log Z$. Therefore $S(r)=k_{\mathrm B}(\beta\bar E+\log Z-D)\le k_{\mathrm B}(\beta\bar E+\log Z)=S(q)$ by the finite identity in [F3]. Equality holds only when $D=0$, which by step 1.1 is equivalent to $r=q$. This proves the unique maximum. [F1, F2, F3, A1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §4.6.2 (printed pp. 216–217)

items.title: General quantum Gibbs normalization and canonical identities
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice and the canonical Gibbs-preparation assumption [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]]. Restrict to its $G=H$ branch: the declared energy operator $H$ is self-adjoint, bounded below, and measured in joules; $T>0$ is in kelvins, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ is in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, and $K_\beta=e^{-\beta H}$ has $0<Z_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}K_\beta<\infty$. Suppose also that on an open interval $J_\beta\subset(0,\infty)$ containing $\beta$, every compact $C\subset J_\beta$ admits a summable family $a_j\ge0$ with $(1+|E_j|^2)e^{-\gamma E_j}\le a_j$ for all energy eigenvalues $E_j$ and $\gamma\in C$. For the adopted density $\rho_\beta=K_\beta/Z_\beta$, the mean and variance of $H$ are finite and
$$-\partial_\beta\log Z_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\beta H),\qquad \partial_\beta^2\log Z_\beta=\operatorname{Var}_{\rho_\beta}(H),\qquad S_{\mathrm{vN}}(\rho_\beta)=k_{\mathrm B}\bigl(\log Z_\beta+\beta\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\beta H)\bigr).$$
Thus $F_{\mathrm{stat}}=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\beta H)-T S_{\mathrm{vN}}(\rho_\beta)$. This statement does not extend the Helmholtz interpretation to an effective generator $H-\mu\mathcal N$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A nonzero quantum Hilbert space, a self-adjoint energy operator $H$ bounded below, a positive assigned temperature, the adopted Gibbs preparation, a finite positive trace, and the local summable moment envelope.

[F1] [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]]: for a declared $G=H$ model with self-adjoint semibounded generator and $0<\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H}<\infty$, the adopted preparation is $\rho_\beta=e^{-\beta H}/Z_\beta$; the postulate explicitly assumes AC and Countable Choice and does not assert equilibration.

[F2] [[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]] and [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]: in the finite-sector class, $S=k_{\mathrm B}s$ and $\beta=1/(k_{\mathrm B}T)$; the general quantum model assigns energy and temperature units but does not by itself identify a trace functional with a macroscopic state function.

[L1] [[thm-tdmath-general-trace-gibbs-model]] (current batch 11 draft): for a semibounded self-adjoint operator with trace-class Gibbs exponential and the stated local moment envelope, the Gibbs weight has a countable energy eigenfamily and the normalized eigenvalue law satisfies the summable canonical mean, variance, and entropy identities. Its full current proof was inspected; its draft status remains conditional.

items.title: Partition, Gibbs-entropy and free-energy factorization for independent finite systems
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Let two finite microstate models from [[def-td-finite-microstate-model]] have nonempty state sets $\Omega_A,\Omega_B$, energies $E_A,E_B$ in joules, and the same $T>0$. Assume their declared composite model has state set $\Omega_A\times\Omega_B$ and energy $E_{AB}(x,y)=E_A(x)+E_B(y)$, with no interaction term. Under the canonical sampling assumption [[post-td-canonical-sampling]], the partition function factorizes as $Z_{AB}=Z_AZ_B$, the joint canonical law is $P_{AB}=P_AP_B$, the Gibbs entropy satisfies $S_{AB}=S_A+S_B$, and the statistical free-energy value satisfies $F_{AB}=F_A+F_B$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Two finite nonempty state sets, additive composite energy, fixed $T>0$, and the canonical preparations of both subsystems and their composite.

[F1] [[def-td-finite-microstate-model]]: each state set is finite and nonempty and the composite state set and additive energy are declared model data.

[F2] [[post-td-canonical-sampling]]: for each model, $P(x)=e^{-\beta E(x)}/Z$ with $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$.

[F3] [[pthm-td-finite-canonical-identities]]: $S=-k_{\mathrm B}\sum_xP(x)\log P(x)$ and $F=\bar E-TS=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z$ for each finite model.

## Proof

**Given:** The finite product state set, additive energy, and the three canonical laws.

1.1 For every $(x,y)\in\Omega_A\times\Omega_B$, $e^{-\beta E_{AB}(x,y)}=e^{-\beta E_A(x)}e^{-\beta E_B(y)}$. Reindexing the finite sum over the Cartesian product therefore gives $Z_{AB}=(\sum_xe^{-\beta E_A(x)})(\sum_ye^{-\beta E_B(y)})=Z_AZ_B$. Dividing the product weight by $Z_AZ_B$ gives $P_{AB}(x,y)=P_A(x)P_B(y)$. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 Since each probability is positive, $\log P_{AB}(x,y)=\log P_A(x)+\log P_B(y)$. Summing against $P_A(x)P_B(y)$ and using the finite normalizations yields $S_{AB}=S_A+S_B$. The mean energy is $\bar E_{AB}=\bar E_A+\bar E_B$ by the same finite factorization, so $F_{AB}=\bar E_{AB}-TS_{AB}=F_A+F_B$. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

In addition to the definition's $C^2$ regularity, assume its numerical Hamiltonian $\hat H$ is $C^\infty$ and its Hamiltonian flow $\phi_t$ is an invertible smooth map of the whole band for every $t\in\mathbb R$. Then, conditional on the current batch-12 draft mathematical interfaces [[thm-tdmath-hamiltonian-measure-and-recurrence]] and [[thm-tdmath-regular-energy-shell-measure]], every shell probability $\nu_{\hat E}$ is invariant:
$$\nu_{\hat E}(\phi_t^{-1}(A))=\nu_{\hat E}(A)$$
for every Borel set $A\subseteq\Sigma_{\hat E}$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$. This result asserts no ergodicity, time-average equality, or thermalization.

**Given:** A canonical Hamiltonian chart, a nonempty compact regular energy shell, its normalized coarea preparation, and a globally defined invertible flow on the band.

items.title: Measurable canonical identities for a dimensionless reference measure
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a measure space with dimensionless reference measure, let $E:X\to\mathbb R\,\mathrm J$ be measurable, and let $J_\beta\subset(0,\infty)$ be open. Suppose $Z(\beta)=\int_Xe^{-\beta E}\,d\mu$ is positive and finite on $J_\beta$, and for each compact $K\subset J_\beta$ there is an integrable $G_K\ge0$ with $(1+|E|^2)e^{-\beta E}\le G_K$ for every $\beta\in K$. Under the canonical sampling assumption [[post-td-canonical-sampling]], define $p_\beta=e^{-\beta E}/Z$, $\langle E\rangle_\beta=\int E p_\beta\,d\mu$, and $\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E)=\int(E-\langle E\rangle_\beta)^2p_\beta\,d\mu$. Then $Z\in C^2$, $-\partial_\beta\log Z=\langle E\rangle_\beta$, $\partial_\beta^2\log Z=\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E)$, and the relative Gibbs entropy is finite with $S_\beta=-k_{\mathrm B}\int p_\beta\log p_\beta\,d\mu=k_{\mathrm B}(\log Z+\beta\langle E\rangle_\beta)$. Hence $F_{\mathrm{stat}}=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z=\langle E\rangle_\beta-TS_\beta$ for $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A dimensionless measure space, a measurable energy, positive finite partition integrals, the canonical density, and the stated local integrable envelope.

[F1] [[def-tdmath-measure-integral]]: measurable nonnegative energies and their nonnegative integrals are interpreted on the specified measure space; signed integrals require absolute integrability.

[F2] [[post-td-canonical-sampling]]: with $0<Z(\beta)<\infty$, the density $p_\beta=e^{-\beta E}/Z$ is the adopted canonical preparation relative to $\mu$.

[L1] [[thm-tdmath-measurable-canonical-identities]] (current batch 11 draft): under the stated $Z$ and compact-interval domination hypotheses, $Z$ is $C^2$, the mean and variance are its log derivatives, and the relative entropy is finite with value $\log Z+\beta\langle E\rangle$. Its full current proof was inspected; its draft status remains conditional.

[F3] [[def-td-si-quantities]]: $E$ and $\langle E\rangle$ are in joules, $T$ is in kelvins, and $k_{\mathrm B}$ is in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, so $\beta$ is in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$.

[A1] The reference measure is dimensionless, $Z$ is positive finite on the open interval, and $(1+|E|^2)e^{-\beta E}$ has the local integrable envelope stated in the Statement.

## Proof

**Given:** The dimensionless reference measure, the measurable energy, the normalized canonical density, and the local envelope.

1.1 The hypotheses in the Statement match [L1], including positive finite $Z$ and the integrable envelope on each compact parameter interval. The density in [F2] is therefore normalized and has finite first and second energy moments. [F1, F2, F3, L1, A1]

2.1 Applying [L1] yields the $C^2$ partition integral, logarithmic mean and variance identities, and the finite relative entropy formula. Multiplying the dimensionless entropy by $k_{\mathrm B}$ gives $S_\beta=k_{\mathrm B}(\log Z+\beta\langle E\rangle_\beta)$; since $\beta k_{\mathrm B}=1/T$, rearranging gives $F_{\mathrm{stat}}=\langle E\rangle_\beta-TS_\beta=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z$. This conclusion is conditional on the draft mathematical supplier. [F2, F3, L1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

items.statement:
Adopt the quantum Gibbs preparation of [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] for a finite list of independent modes at $T>0$. Its partition trace and mean occupation are
$$Z_B=(1-q)^{-1},\qquad \langle N\rangle_B=\frac{q}{1-q}=\frac1{e^{\beta\varepsilon}-1}.$$
For a fermionic two-level occupation system with energies $0,\varepsilon$, the partition sum and excited-state occupation are
$$Z_F=1+q,\qquad \langle N\rangle_F=\frac{q}{1+q}=\frac1{e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1}.$$
For a finite independent collection, the corresponding partition traces multiply and each mode's marginal mean is the displayed one. These are exact model identities under the adopted preparation.

**Given:** The finite independent mode models, positive mode energies, assigned $T>0$, and the adopted Gibbs preparation.

Its full proof was inspected; the published carrier lacks the required audit marker, so this use remains escalated.

[F5] [[pthm-td-independent-factorization]]: for an explicitly independent finite product model, partition functions factor and the product canonical law has the subsystem marginals.

[F6] [[def-td-si-quantities]] and [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]: $\varepsilon$ is in joules, $T$ in kelvins, $\beta$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, and the occupation number is dimensionless.

items.title: Cesaro dephasing for a discrete trace-class quantum model

items.statement:

$$\bar\rho_\tau:=\frac1{\tau}\int_0^\tau U_t\rho_0U_t^*\,dt$$

The finite canonical, maximum-entropy, independent-factorization and finite-bath claims concern the exact finite state spaces and shell-weight assumptions stated in their items. Countable and measurable derivative identities require their local summable or integrable moment envelopes; a lower energy bound alone does not normalize the partition function. The lattice bulk-pressure and concentration claims apply only to the bounded finite-range lattice model and, for concentration, a differentiability point of the limiting log-partition density. The page-level continuum-pressure prerequisite is a distinct interaction model; no stable-tempered continuum limit is inferred from the lattice theorem.

The classical shell result applies only to a nonempty compact regular level with the coarea normalization and a globally defined invertible flow on the stated band. It does not imply ergodicity or equality of long-time averages with the shell law. The quantum trace identities require a semibounded self-adjoint generator, a positive finite Gibbs trace and the stated moment envelope; discrete dephasing is a trace-norm Cesaro limit with degenerate eigenspaces retained, not pointwise relaxation or a Gibbs limit.

Boltzmann microstate entropy, finite Gibbs entropy, von Neumann entropy and the macroscopic entropy function are distinct objects until a model supplies an explicit identification. The statistical value $-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z$ is not silently identified with a macroscopic Helmholtz or grand potential. Canonical and microcanonical sampling are adopted preparation assumptions. None of the finite probability identities, continuum or lattice pressure limits, shell-invariance results or quantum trace calculations reports an experiment or establishes that nature follows the model.

items.title: One bosonic and one fermionic mode at a specified temperature
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Choose $T>0$ and excitation energy $\varepsilon=k_{\mathrm B}T\log 2$ joules, so $q=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}=1/2$. Consider separately one bosonic mode with occupations $n=0,1,2,\ldots$ and one fermionic mode with occupations $n=0,1$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The declared one-mode systems, their positive excitation energy, and the adopted Gibbs preparation.

[F1] [[pthm-td-finite-mode-occupation-and-trace-formulas]]: for $q=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$, the bosonic partition trace is $(1-q)^{-1}$ with mean $q/(1-q)$, and the fermionic partition sum is $1+q$ with excited occupation $q/(1+q)$; these are conditional on its stated quantum preparation and suppliers.

[F2] [[def-td-si-quantities]]: $T$ is in kelvins, $k_{\mathrm B}$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, and $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$.

[A1] The selected energy is $\varepsilon=k_{\mathrm B}T\log 2>0$ joules, and $q=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}=1/2$.

## Verification

**Given:** $q=1/2$ and the finite-mode identities in [F1].

1.1 The bosonic trace is $Z_B=(1-1/2)^{-1}=2$, and the probability of occupation $n$ is $2^{-(n+1)}$. Its mean occupation is $(1/2)/(1-1/2)=1$. [given, F1, F2, A1, algebra]

2.1 The fermionic partition sum is $Z_F=1+1/2=3/2$, so the ground and excited probabilities are $2/3$ and $1/3$, respectively, and the mean occupation is $1/3$. The bosonic and fermionic values belong to distinct declared models. [F1, F2, A1, algebra] ∎

Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§5.6–5.7

items.title: Two independent two-level sites give a product thermal law
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Let each site have states $0,1$ with energies $0,\varepsilon$, and take $T>0$ with $\varepsilon=k_{\mathrm B}T\log 2$. The composite has states $(n_1,n_2)\in\{0,1\}^2$ and additive energy $E=\varepsilon(n_1+n_2)$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Two finite sites, additive energy, common positive temperature, and canonical sampling.

[F1] [[def-td-finite-microstate-model]]: the composite state set is the Cartesian product and additivity of energy is explicit model data.

[F2] [[pthm-td-finite-canonical-identities]]: each finite canonical law has probabilities proportional to $e^{-\beta E}$.

[F3] [[pthm-td-independent-factorization]]: under the explicit product and additive-energy assumptions, partition sums factor and the joint canonical law is the product of the two subsystem laws.

[A1] Set $\beta\varepsilon=\log 2$, hence the single-site excited-state weight is $q=1/2$.

## Verification

**Given:** The model data and $q=1/2$.

1.1 Each site has $Z_1=1+q=3/2$ and probabilities $(2/3,1/3)$. By [F3], $Z_{12}=Z_1^2=9/4$ and the joint probabilities of $(00,01,10,11)$ are $(4/9,2/9,2/9,1/9)$. [F1, F2, F3, A1, algebra]

2.1 The expected total occupation is the sum of the two marginal means, $1/3+1/3=2/3$, so the mean energy is $2\varepsilon/3$. This conclusion follows for the declared noninteracting product model only. [F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §1.3.1
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.4.1 and 4.6

items.title: Identical bosonic modes do not have a finite infinite-mode Gibbs trace
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Take modes indexed by $j\in\mathbb N$, each with excitation energy $\varepsilon>0$, and let $q=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}\in(0,1)$. Let $\mathcal F$ be the set of finite-support occupation sequences $n=(n_j)_{j\ge1}$ with $n_j\in\mathbb N_0$. Fix its enumeration by increasing $R(n)=\sum_{j:n_j>0}(j+n_j)$, breaking ties lexicographically by the finite list of nonzero pairs $(j,n_j)$; for each bound on $R$, only finitely many configurations occur. On $\ell^2(\mathcal F)$ with its occupation basis $|n\rangle$, define the bounded positive diagonal Gibbs weight $K_\beta|n\rangle=q^{\sum_jn_j}|n\rangle$. On the subspace with $n_j=0$ for every $j>M$, the corresponding finite-mode partition sum is the trace of that restriction.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The independent identical-mode Fock model, positive $\beta\varepsilon$, and the canonical trace convention.

[F1] [[pthm-td-finite-mode-occupation-and-trace-formulas]]: for each finite collection of independent bosonic modes the Gibbs trace is the product of the one-mode traces $(1-q)^{-1}$.

[F2] [[post-td-canonical-sampling]]: the A-page countable canonical law is adopted only for a specified countable model with a positive finite partition sum.

[F3] [[def-countable-choice]], [[def-trace-class-operator]], and [[thm-trace-of-a-positive-operator-is-the-sum-of-its-eigenvalues]]: under Countable Choice, a positive trace-class operator has finite trace equal to the sum of its nonnegative eigenvalues with multiplicity.

[F4] [[def-tdmath-countable-canonical-model]]: the nonnegative countable partition sum is the supremum of its finite subsums, so a finite normalizer bounds the sum over every subset of the listed states.

[F5] [[def-td-si-quantities]]: $\varepsilon$ is in joules and $\beta$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, so $\beta\varepsilon$ is dimensionless.

[A1] The basis indices are all finite-support occupation sequences with physical energy $E_n=\varepsilon\sum_jn_j$ joules, so their Gibbs eigenvalues are $e^{-\beta E_n}=q^{\sum_jn_j}$; every finite-mode subset is a subset of this full basis.

## Verification

**Given:** $0<q<1$ and the finite-mode subspaces described above.

1.1 The trace contribution from states supported on the first $M$ modes is the finite product $Z_M=(1-q)^{-M}$ by [F1]. Since $c=(1-q)^{-1}>1$, $Z_M=c^M$ is unbounded: writing $c=1+r$ with $r>0$, induction gives $(1+r)^M\ge1+Mr$. The unit convention [F5] makes $\beta\varepsilon$ dimensionless. [F1, A1, F5, algebra]

2.1 If $K_\beta$ were trace class, [F3] would make its positive eigenvalue sum finite and equal to its trace. For each $M$, the configurations with $n_j=0$ for $j>M$ form a subset of the enumerated states [A1]; [F4] therefore makes their finite-mode partition sum $Z_M$ no larger than the full normalizer. [F1] identifies that subset sum as $Z_M$, and step 1.1 makes $Z_M$ unbounded, a contradiction. Hence $K_\beta$ is not trace class and the countable partition sum has no finite value. The preparation condition [F2] fails, so this model has no normalized countable canonical law of the stated form. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §§3.5–3.6
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§5.6–5.7

items.title: An identity dynamics leaves a noncanonical finite preparation unchanged
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Let $\Omega=\{a,b\}$ with energies $E_a=0$, $E_b=\varepsilon>0$, and fix $T>0$. The separately adopted canonical law has probabilities proportional to $(1,e^{-\beta\varepsilon})$. For the dynamical comparison, stipulate the identity transition map $\Phi_t(a)=a$, $\Phi_t(b)=b$ for all $t\ge0$ and start with the point mass $\delta_a$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A two-state energy model, positive temperature, the canonical preparation rule, and the explicitly stipulated identity dynamics.

[F1] [[def-td-finite-microstate-model]]: the two microstates and their fixed finite energies define an admissible finite statistical model.

[F2] [[post-td-canonical-sampling]]: the canonical probabilities are the normalized weights $e^{-\beta E_x}$; this is an adopted preparation rule and includes no time-evolution equation.

[A1] The comparison dynamics is the deterministic identity map $\Phi_t$ for every $t\ge0$, and the initial law for that comparison is $\delta_a$.

## Verification

**Given:** $\varepsilon>0$, $T>0$, and the stipulated dynamics.

1.1 Put $q=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$, so $0<q<1$. The canonical law is $P_\beta(a)=1/(1+q)$ and $P_\beta(b)=q/(1+q)$; in particular it is not $\delta_a$. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 The identity map preserves the initial point mass at every time: $(\Phi_t)_*\delta_a=\delta_a$. Hence the time-evolved law does not converge to the canonical law, whose probability of $b$ is strictly positive. This is a counterexample to deriving equilibration from the sampling rule alone. [A1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §1.3
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.4–4.6

items.title: Two isolated two-level sites do not relax an energy eigenstate to Gibbs form
items.design_state: Complete draft carrier authored; scoped checks and prerequisite acceptance remain pending.
items.statement:
Take two noninteracting two-level sites with states $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$, single-site energies $0,\varepsilon$, and total Hamiltonian $H=\varepsilon(n_1+n_2)$. Fix $T>0$ and $\varepsilon=k_{\mathrm B}T\log2$. Start in $\rho_0=|00\rangle\langle00|$ and adopt the closed-system unitary evolution generated by $H$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The finite product energy model, the assigned positive temperature, the unitary evolution postulate, and the stated initial state.

[F1] [[pthm-td-independent-factorization]]: for two explicitly independent finite systems with additive energy, the canonical joint law is the product of the single-site canonical laws.

[F2] [[pthm-td-finite-mode-occupation-and-trace-formulas]]: a fermionic two-level site with $q=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$ has excited probability $q/(1+q)$ under the adopted quantum Gibbs preparation.

[F3] [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] and [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]: closed-system evolution is $\rho(t)=U_t\rho_0U_t^*$ with $U_t=e^{-itH/\hbar}$.

[A1] Each site has $q=1/2$, and the initial vector is the ground energy eigenvector $|00\rangle$ of $H$.

## Verification

**Given:** $q=1/2$, the product model, and the closed-system evolution.

1.1 By [F1]–[F2], the finite-temperature Gibbs probabilities on $(00,01,10,11)$ are $(4/9,2/9,2/9,1/9)$. In particular the Gibbs probability of $|11\rangle$ is $1/9>0$. [F1, F2, A1, algebra]

2.1 Since $H|00\rangle=0$, $U_t|00\rangle=|00\rangle$ for every $t$; thus $\rho(t)=|00\rangle\langle00|$. Its probability for the projector $|11\rangle\langle11|$ is zero at every time, unlike the Gibbs value $1/9$. The state therefore never reaches this Gibbs density under the declared unitary evolution. [F3, A1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §§1.3.1 and 3.6
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.3–4.4 and §5.7
